title: AutoKernel loop core
summary: The production path is `serial_run.main`. It launches `python -m ...loop.run` as a batch child (serial_run.py:1266). That runs `run.main`, then `pool.drive`, then `pipeline.run_pool`, then `loop.iterate`. pool.py and pipeline.py are small and well documented; the debt sits in three places. (1) `run.main` is one function of 5,518 lines with cyclomatic complexity 1,166. It holds 92 nested closures, 116 CLI flags, 15 places that overwrite parsed args, and 124 branches on legacy / GPU-serving / CPU target mode. Because the closures cannot be called on their own, 28 test files grep run.py's source text instead of testing behaviour, and two of them fail today. (2) A complete second control plane sits inside loop/: campaign_control, worker_lifecycle, unified_worker, unified_driver and the standalone_* modules, about 15.7k source lines plus 9.5k test lines. It is never instantiated from the production entry points, its service unit is marked "deliberately not installable", and it has had no commits since 2026-09-09 while the legacy loop files got 242. The legacy path is still tied to it through small helpers and lazy imports. (3) The guards CI workflow is `disabled_manually` on GitHub: the last of its 249 runs was on 2026-09-09 and the last pass was 2026-09-01. Even when it ran, an earlier guard step failed first, so the loop-package test step was skipped; the 451 failures found on 2026-10-07 built up with no CI watching. Two real bugs: `run._git` ignores git's exit code, including on the `reset --hard` that restores a tip after an interaction regression, so a failed reset makes the loop record a measurement under the wrong tip. And the scope-gap hook runs on every 30-second heartbeat, which breaks its own "never on every iteration" contract. There is also duplication across loop/: about 1,260 lines of copy-pasted validators (`_digest` 36 copies, `_text` 36, `_sha` 32, `_canonical` 31 in 18 variants) and 13 different git wrappers. Semicolon-compressed code (E702/E701) does not occur in any of the 11 C1 files; the 597 E702 are in controller/ and its tests. Bloat estimate: about 1,450 lines can go now with evidence (validators, dead and test-only code, callback forwarding, git wrappers), plus about 25.2k lines if the operator retires the undeployed standalone stack. The total is about 26.6k lines.

findings.title: BUG: run._git ignores git's exit status, including on `reset --hard` that restores the accumulator tip after an interaction regression
findings.evidence: run.py:1693-1695: `return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600).stdout.strip()` has no returncode check. It is used for state changes and identities: `_git(args.worktree, "reset", "--hard", previous_tip)` (4985), `worktree add --detach` (5200), and rev-parse HEAD for current_anchor_commit (4793), the accumulator `head` (4892) and promote_anchor's champion_commit (4786). Failure scenario: a stale `.git/worktrees/<wt>/index.lock` left by a killed lane makes the reset exit 128 ('Unable to create index.lock: File exists'). Nothing notices. promote_anchor() (4775) then builds args.worktree (build_champion compiles `args.worktree`, 4651), which is still the regressing commit, and pool.promote_anchor records champion_commit=HEAD. `persist_comparison(restored, "restored-prior-tip", measured_tip=previous_tip)` (4988-4989) then files the regressing build's measurement labelled as previous_tip. If that reads non-negative, bundle[0].compounded_bench_pct is set from it with MEASUREMENT_CURRENT and saved (4994-4997). A failed rev-parse also returns "", which names evidence files '-initial-<id>.json' (4910).
findings.proposal: Give run._git `check=True` by default, raising RuntimeError with the first 400 chars of stderr, and add an explicit `check=False` only where failure is tolerated. After the reset at 4985, assert `_git(args.worktree, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD') == previous_tip` before promote_anchor(). Fold into the shared git helper (C1-12).
findings.verification: New unit test: a temp git repo with an index.lock in place; calling run._git(repo, 'reset', '--hard', sha) must raise. Then cd /workspace/repos/epyc-inference-research && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q scripts/kernel_rnd/autokernel/loop/test_existing_cpu_run.py scripts/kernel_rnd/autokernel/loop/test_keep_overhead.py scripts/kernel_rnd/autokernel/loop/test_accumulate.py scripts/kernel_rnd/autokernel/loop/test_gates.py.
findings.verify_reason: run.py:1693-1695 is exactly as quoted: no returncode check. `_git(args.worktree, "reset", "--hard", previous_tip)` at 4985 is unverified; promote_anchor follows at 4986-4990, and it builds args.worktree (gates.compiles(args.worktree, ...) at 4651) and records champion_commit=_git(... rev-parse HEAD) (4786). Then comes persist_comparison(restored, 'restored-prior-tip', measured_tip=previous_tip). The scenario holds. One correction: the `worktree add` at 5200 IS verified right after it (5201-5203 compare rev-parse HEAD against commit and check status, raising ValueError), so it is not an unchecked site. The finder missed more fail-open sites from the same root cause: `status --porcelain` checks at 5160, 5202 and 5246 read a git failure ('' on stdout) as a clean tree. In ppl_contract_evict_culprit, a failing `rev-list` at 5248 yields shas=[] and so returns {'result':'no_suspect'} (5253). After the reset at 4985, assert HEAD == previous_tip before promote_anchor(). In ppl_contract_evict_culprit, map a git failure to {'result':'held_unavailable'}, never 'no_suspect'. Add timeouts to the raw revert and revert --abort calls (5289-5292). Fold into the C1-12 helper.

findings.title: BUG: scope-gap stagnation hook runs on every 30 s heartbeat; non-atomically rewrites scope_gap.json and floods stdout, contradicting its contract
findings.evidence: run.publish (5440-5458) calls `roofline_coverage.stagnation_scope_gap_hook(...)` on every call and prints `profile   STAGNATION + UNCOVERED ROOFLINE GAP: wrote {path}` whenever it writes. WorkerStatusPublisher._heartbeat (heartbeat.py:141-151) re-invokes that same writer every HEARTBEAT_S=30 s (run.py:30). write_scope_gap's docstring (roofline_coverage.py:359) says 'Called from the stagnation hook, never on every iteration'. It writes with plain `target.write_text(...)` (367), not atomically, and stamps generated_at=now. Once a target is stagnant and the gap triggered: scope_gap.json is rewritten every 30 s (a human or dashboard can read a truncated file, and generated_at no longer records first detection), and stdout gets about 2,880 identical lines a day. serial_run keeps only a 1 MiB tail per child stream (MAX_SERIAL_CHILD_LOG_BYTES_PER_STREAM, serial_run.py:32), so this pushes real warnings out. The hook's own docstring (374-380) also says a malformed uncovered_gap 'still raises ... not swallow', yet run.py wraps it in `except Exception ... # pragma: no cover - defensive, observe-only` (5456).
findings.proposal: Call the hook from the per-outcome record path (after `latest.append`), not from publish. Write only on a transition (not-stagnant to stagnant, or a changed uncovered_gap digest), using status.write_json (atomic). Print once per transition. Either let a malformed gap raise as documented or record it as a structured degradation (C1-18). Remove the `pragma: no cover`.

findings.title: Each 30 s heartbeat materialises every outcome's full Comparison (documented as up to 100 MB) up to three times and forks git under the publisher lock, but uses only 4 scalars
findings.evidence: Each publish builds `[o.to_attempt() for o in outcomes]` twice, once for the scope-gap hook (5450) and once for status.write (5466), and actor_health builds it again for the last 60 (5431). Outcome.to_attempt (loop.py:578-580) embeds `self.comparison.to_dict()`. status.py:41-46 records that Comparison.to_dict 'carries the complete measurement lifecycle, including every residency sample from both arms ... made a five-pair CPU guard exceed 100 MB'. Yet status.write (status.py:206-300) reads only status, mechanism_id, effect_fraction and reason from each row (counts, `recent`, stagnation_signal, abstain_rate). publish also runs `_git(args.worktree, "rev-parse", "HEAD")` (5465), a fork with a 600 s timeout, on every call. All of this runs inside WorkerStatusPublisher's RLock (heartbeat.py:145), so any of the 28 main-thread publish() calls waits behind a heartbeat. This is hot: it fires every 30 s for the life of the run, including during A/B measurement windows, and every stage boundary adds more calls.
findings.proposal: Add `Outcome.status_row()` returning {status, mechanism_id, effect_fraction, reason} plus gate status. Compute it once per publish and pass it to stagnation_signal, the hook and status.write; status.write's contract already takes Mappings. Cache the champion head in RunSession and update it where current_anchor_commit[0] is set (4793) and after commit/reset, instead of forking git per publish. The loop-run.json terminal write keeps the full to_attempt().

title: AutoKernel loop periphery (the regrowth)
summary: loop/ holds 171 files and 95.6k code lines (my AST count; the guard reports 95,260). It is really two systems. One is the live run.py/serial_run lanes (DS41 and Q38FN). The other is a "unified/standalone" replacement architecture: about 80 modules landed on 2026-09-09, the operator rejected it as a replacement that same day ("extend the working loop; do not replace it", unified-surface-program.md:17), and nothing has launched it since the 2026-09-11 scoped trial. I walked symbol-level reachability from every real entry point: run, serial_run, resume, the hand-run fold instruments, the 16 scripts/benchmark importers, actor_tools_mcp and the gdb probes. Type annotations and source-identity registries were ignored because they hash code but never run it. The walk finds 57 modules (29.7k LOC) with zero executable code. campaign_control (4.7k) and worker_lifecycle (2.5k) are each live for only about 100 lines. Five thin bridges keep all of this attached to the live import path, including an annotation-only CampaignController in the HTTP transport and a 2-line private _target_digest. The three biggest problems are: (1) that dead architecture plus about 26k LOC of its tests, which produced 357 of the 451 loop failures on 2026-10-07; (2) the autokernel CI workflow has been disabled_manually since 2026-09-09T22:31Z, and its last run failed before the regrowth guard and the loop tests ever ran — so established fact (c) understates it: nothing runs at all; (3) a 2,560-line code budget nobody can satisfy, plus guarded docs (README, FOOTPRINT) that no longer describe the package; FOOTPRINT's own coverage test fails with 206 modules missing. Bloat estimate: about 45k source LOC removable (36.5k as whole files, about 7k as dead branches in 13 mixed modules, plus small one-offs), about 27k test LOC, and about 3.8k lines of stale design docs. findings.title: Hand-maintained source_identity registries keep dead entry points referenced and turn refactors into evidence invalidation
findings.evidence: 20 modules carry source_identity/_source_closure registries, 516 lines in total. cpu_profile.py:229-296 lists 45 callables by name, including run_profile_request and main, which only the dead unified profile worker uses; it also hashes 12 files and the 6.5 MB interpreter binary. runtime_admission.py:52-68 lists _cpu_arm and _rebind_build_dso from run.py. Identities are re-checked against retained records (cpu_profile.py:348, 711, 1336, 1415; runtime_admission.py:406, 756). So moving a listed function (C2-03, C2-16) changes its module/qualname and retained profiles and admissions are refused: a behaviour-preserving refactor becomes a recalibration. The registries also defeat static dead-code tools: plain reachability counts ~80k of 95.6k lines as live, against ~55k executable. The measured cost is small (cpu_profile 33 ms per call, runtime_admission 16 ms), so this is about coupling, not speed.
findings.proposal: Replace the per-callable lists with one helper, lifecycle_observation.module_closure(modules, constants), that hashes the declared module files, and drop the dead entries now. Document in loop/README that refactoring a pinned module starts a new measurement epoch (epoch_aliases.py already supports this), so such refactors are planned rather than accidental.
findings.verification: Each module's identity tests pass. Retained-record reopen tests (cpu_profile reopen; runtime_admission restore_selection) pass with regenerated fixtures. Reachability without stripping registries now matches executable reachability (c2_syms vs c2_exec within 1%).
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: 15 non-test loop modules define source_identity or _source_closure. cpu_profile.py:229-296 pins main and run_profile_request, hashes 12 files including worker_lifecycle.py and the benchmark script, and hashes the interpreter binary. runtime_admission.py:50-68 pins run._cpu_arm and _rebind_build_dso by callable identity. The proposed fix is worse than the problem. lifecycle_observation.callable_identity (:349) and _code_projection (:273-298) hash bytecode, constants, names and the exception table without line numbers, so a pin survives unrelated edits to its file. runtime_admission deliberately pins two run.py callables and does not hash run.py, the 7,395-line, most-edited file. Replacing callable pins with module_closure(file hashes) would invalidate every retained admission on any run.py edit. That increases evidence invalidation; it does not reduce it. The registries do tie C2-01 and C2-16 together, and that is the real point.
findings.corrected_proposal: Keep the callable-level pins. In the C2-01 epoch bump, remove the dead roles and files from cpu_profile.source_identity (main, run_profile_request, worker_lifecycle.py, run_autokernel_cpu_profile.py). If moves should not invalidate evidence, exclude module and qualname from the hashed identity body (they are the only location-dependent fields) under a new identity schema, registered through epoch_aliases.

findings.title: api._resolve_effect ignores which hypothesis the e-value tested: a non-inferiority e-value is labelled IMPROVEMENT, and REGRESSION is effectively unreachable
findings.evidence: `_resolve_effect` runs `if effect.e_value < effect.threshold: EVIDENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD`, then `improving = effect.value > 0 ...; return IMPROVEMENT if improving else REGRESSION`. EffectEstimate (api.py:1355) has no hypothesis field. PairedBlockReducer.reduce runs `run_e_process(oriented, ..., hypothesis=campaign.hypothesis, margin=campaign.margin)` (statistics.py:3391) and stores `e_value=e_run.e_running_max` (line 3461). CampaignStatistics accepts any value in HYPOTHESES (line 3071), and the loop's statistical declaration (serving_preparation.py:187) only validates `st.null_boundary_for(self.hypothesis, self.margin)`. Failure scenario: a campaign declared with hypothesis=non_inferiority and margin=0.02. A candidate with median +1.2% (above phi and the MDE) whose blocks mostly beat -2% crosses 1/alpha. It is resolved IMPROVEMENT and becomes speed-rank-admissible, although the e-process only showed 'not worse than -2%'. In the other direction, an improvement e-process can only cross when most oriented blocks are positive, which makes the median positive. REGRESSION therefore needs e >= threshold with median <= 0 and is practically unreachable. A significant slowdown is reported as EVIDENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD, not REGRESSION.
findings.proposal: Add `hypothesis: str` (and margin) to api.EffectEstimate and serialise both. In _resolve_effect, return IMPROVEMENT only when hypothesis == improvement and value is on the improving side; return a separate NON_INFERIOR resolution, not rankable, for non-inferiority. Either drop REGRESSION or compute it from a second e-process on the negated orientation. Set the field in PairedBlockReducer and control_runner.reduce_live_blocks. findings.title: Small statistics defects: min_samples_for_quantile float rounding, and a dead variance branch obscuring the betting rule
findings.evidence: min_samples_for_quantile returns `int(math.ceil(1.0 / tail))` with `tail = min(q, 1-q)`. Measured: q=0.9 gives 1/0.09999999999999998 = 10.000000000000002, so ceil is 11. q=0.8 gives 6 instead of 5. q=0.1 gives 10, so the function is asymmetric for the same tail. The only current callers use 0.95 and 0.975 (lines 1801, 1859, 2161), which happen to round correctly (20 and 40), so the defect is latent. lambda_from_moments (lines 889-907) computes `var = total_sq/count - mean^2; denom = var + mean^2`. The statistic is a sign in {-1, +1}, so total_sq == count and denom is always exactly 1. The `denom <= 0` branch is unreachable, and the betting fraction is simply clip(mean of past signs, 0, cap). The docstring's 'mean over second moment' hides that, although it is the fact behind the documented 5.5687 ceiling: (1+0.1)·(1+0.5)^4.
findings.proposal: Compute the bound exactly with `fractions.Fraction(q).limit_denominator()` (or `math.ceil(1/tail - 1e-9)`) and add tests for q in {0.8, 0.9, 0.1}. Simplify lambda_from_moments to `min(max(total/count, 0.0), cap)` for count > 0, and state the closed form in the docstring. Wealth series stay bit-identical for ±1 inputs.

findings.evidence: journal.py:1195-1202: 'try: if __package__: from .loop.a2_execution_state import validate_transition ... validate_transition(payload) except Exception as exc: out.append(f"A2 runtime execution transition: {exc}")'. Reproduced from scripts/kernel_rnd with sys.modules['yaml']=None (the CI runner's real condition, C5-01): J._validate_native_payload(J.KIND_A2_RUNTIME_EXECUTION, {'schema':'x'}) -> ['A2 runtime execution transition: import of yaml halted; None in sys.modules'], and the same for KIND_MAINTENANCE_EXECUTION. Journal.append() turns that into ValueError '<kind> payload is invalid: ...' (journal.py:2747-2751). Journal.scan(validate_payloads=True) turns it into a JournalDefect 'payload fails validation' for every such line (3196-3205). A dependency or environment fault therefore looks like corrupt durable records. A NameError or AttributeError inside a validator is laundered the same way.

AST: one if/elif chain of 27 branches on `kind` (journal.py:1194-2231). Inline branches validate loop-owned records: KIND_PLANNED_SERVING_ARM_CAPTURED 1299-1477 (178 lines), KIND_CAMPAIGN_SUPERVISOR_EVENT 1570-1755 (185), KIND_CANDIDATE_TRANSACTION 1755-2025 (270). title: AutoKernel test suite [UNVERIFIED: verifier hit usage limit]
summary: The AutoKernel suite is large: 392 test files and 208,614 test LOC against 281,524 source LOC, a 0.74 ratio (loop/ alone is 96k test LOC against 120k source). It collects 11,332 tests, plus 383 in release/test_t3* that cannot be collected at any standard checkout path. Little of that size turns into a gate. The only CI workflow was disabled by hand on 2026-09-10, after 168 consecutive red runs (last green was #81 on 2026-09-01); 347 AutoKernel commits (+63k source, +47k test lines) have landed since with no CI at all. Even when it ran, the floor and regrowth steps failed first, so the 'decision arithmetic' and 5,048-test 'loop package' steps were skipped. A full local run at HEAD gives 476 failed, 87 errors and 10,576 passed in 22m45s on 3 xdist workers. About 58% of the failures depend on the host (CPU count, root uid, /mnt/raid0, /workspace). The rest are real regressions nobody saw: a test-helper signature change breaks 38 tests, a stale 'kept'/'keep_candidate' harness fails, and the footprint/README guard suite is red. The three biggest structural problems: (1) CI cannot run tests: it installs only pytest, has no yaml dependency, and runs everything as one sequential job; (2) tests are tied to the host and to sibling repos (EPYC_ROOT_REPO=/workspace, /mnt/raid0 receipts, jobs=32), and the single conftest does not isolate them; (3) shared fixtures live inside test modules (448 test-to-test imports, and a test function reused as a harness from 33 call sites), modules load under two or three import roots (72 doubled, 4 tripled), and obsolete doc-coupled guard suites (test_campaign_footprint, test_readme) pin stale prose and cost 225 s. About 9,400 LOC can plausibly go: about 2,600 from the obsolete footprint/README doc suites, about 5,800 from a grep-verified test-only source cluster plus its tests, and about 1,000 from fixture deduplication, unittest boilerplate and an AST check that ruff already does. A further about 4,570 LOC of dormant Arena-plane tests depends on an operator decision.

findings.evidence: GitHub API (actions list_workflows): 'autokernel guards' has state=disabled_manually, updated 2026-09-10T00:31+02:00. Of 249 runs, 28 passed. The last green was run #81 (2026-09-01 08:00), followed by 168 consecutive failures. Job steps from the API: run #130 (2026-09-08): 'Regrowth guards' failure, then 'The decision arithmetic' and 'The loop package' skipped. Run #250 (2026-09-09): 'Prove the suites did not silently shrink' failure, with the log showing '1465 tests collected, 54 errors'. findings.title: Test fixture hard-codes 32 build jobs while production refuses jobs > os.cpu_count(): 97 failures on any host under 32 CPUs (GitHub runners have 4)
